newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - ITT Industries knows of no other bidders.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - ITT Industries knows of no other bidders.

text.p: ITT Industries Inc Chairman Travis Engen said Monday his company approached Goulds Pumps Inc about a takeover in March and he was unaware of any rival suitors for the pump manufacturer.
The companies said today they had signed a definitive agreement for ITT Industries to acquire Goulds for $37 per share, or $815 million.
Goulds also announced it had adopted a "poison pill" plan, sparking speculation that it was avoiding a hostile bidder when it agreed to the ITT Industries deal.
Goulds officials were not available for comment.

"This shareholder rights action was agreed to between the parties as part of the acquisition agreement," Engen said in response to a question about why the poison pill was adopted. "It gives Goulds the opportunity to be in more control in the next few months."
Asked if there was another, possibly hostile, party seeking to acquire Goulds, he replied, "We are not aware of anything like that."
He declined to say if the poison pill was intended to ward off any future Goulds takeover bids.
He said he expects the transaction to close in June.

"We have been examining (expansion in) the fluid technology area for quite a while and we identified Goulds as an acquisition candidate and approached them in March," Engen told Reuters in an interview.
In midsession Nasdaq trade, Goulds shares were trading at 36 after climbing 13-1/8, or 57.4 percent, following news of the merger agreement.
ITT Industries shares were up 1/8 to 23-1/2 on the New York Stock Exchange.
